pages.title: A obra e a situação

work.title: Pat-a-Cake
work.note: Pat-a-Cake é uma rima infantil em inglês, associada ao dramaturgo Thomas D'Urfey, que a incluiu numa peça de 1698. Os versos pedem a um padeiro que asse um bolo, e a rima costuma ser acompanhada de palmas. A brincadeira ajuda os bebês a aprender ritmo e movimentos. pages.question: Como a história dessa obra ajuda você a imaginar a situação de hoje? Diga uma ideia em inglês.

facts.label: Situação
facts.sub: In the USA, a party starts with an invitation and a short reply. Learn the little words that make you a great guest, from RSVP to what to bring.

facts.big: RSVP means “please reply to the invitation”.
facts.label: Fato cultural
facts.sub: It comes from the French “répondez, s’il vous plaît”.

facts.big: At a potluck, each guest brings a dish to share.
facts.label: Fato cultural
facts.sub: A potluck is a meal where everybody brings some food.

mini.en: Hi! Can you come to my {party|invite|drink}?
mini.pt: Oi! Você pode vir à minha {festa|convidar|bebida}?

facts.big: You can say “I can’t come” to an invitation.
facts.label: Fato cultural
facts.sub: A short, kind “no” is fine: “I’d love to, but I’m busy.”

facts.label: Educação e tom
facts.sub: Always answer an invitation. Say Thanks for the invite! and ask Can I bring something?

compare.br: In Brazil, friends often just show up and the host does the cooking; a guest may arrive later than the invitation time.
compare.us: In the USA, guests usually reply to the invitation and often bring a drink or a snack to share.
compare.tip: Asking “Can I bring something?” is a kind way to say thank you before the party.
compare.ask: Do you bring something to a party where you live? What do you bring? Say it in English.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: RSVP means “please reply to the invitation”.
items.why: It comes from the French “répondez, s’il vous plaît”.

items.s: It is rude to ask, “Can I bring something?”
items.why: It is polite. Hosts often say, “Just a drink or a snack!”

items.s: At a potluck, each guest brings a dish to share.
items.why: A potluck is a meal where everybody brings some food.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 2/2

items.s: At a birthday party, people never sing.
items.why: People usually sing “Happy Birthday to You” and the person blows out candles.

items.s: You can say “I can’t come” to an invitation.
items.why: A short, kind “no” is fine: “I’d love to, but I’m busy.”

pages.instruction: Mais uma rodada: decida e explique.

pages.title: Come to my party! · 1/3
paragraphs: Hi Nia, **it’ll be fun**! I am having a party on Saturday at eight. It is a small party at my house, and I want you to come.
The address is 123 Oak Street in Oakland. **Can I bring something?** you ask. Sure! A drink or a snack is great. I will make pizza and a big cake. A cake with a bowl of fruit is my favorite.
pages.prompt: Onde começa e o que acontece?

pages.title: Come to my party! · 2/3
paragraphs: We will play music and dance. Some friends play games. At nine, we will sing “Happy Birthday” and the birthday girl will blow out the candles. We say “**Cheers!**” and raise our cups.

Do you know the old rhyme “Pat-a-Cake”? It is an English nursery rhyme from a play of 1698. Children clap and say, “Bake me a cake as fast as you can.” My little brother loves it, and he will sing it at the party.

pages.title: Come to my party! · 3/3
paragraphs: Please tell me by Thursday. Can you come? If you can’t, **I’d love to see you next time**. **Thanks for the invite** is all you need to say. **See you Saturday!**

pages.title: Palavras pelo contexto

items.q: It’ll be fun, so please come! O que significa “fun”?
items.why: Fun = enjoyable.

items.q: I want to blow out the candles. O que significa “blow out”?
items.why: Blow out = stop a flame with air.

items.q: Please tell me by Thursday. O que significa “by Thursday”?
items.why: By = not later than.

pages.instruction: Use a frase inteira como pista.

pages.title: Confira as pistas

items.q: The party starts at nine.
items.why: It starts at eight; they sing at nine.

items.q: Guests can bring a drink or a snack.
items.why: “A drink or a snack is great.”

items.q: Lina’s sister will sing Pat-a-Cake.
items.why: Her little brother will sing it.
